data.name: Asit
data.gender_notes: Asit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Asit is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Asadh’ meaning 'dawn' or 'daybreak'. In Hindu mythology, Asit is a name of the sun god, Surya. It is also the name of one of the nine planets in Hindu astronomy, known as Shukla-Pitr or Sukra, representing the planet Venus. The name Asit carries the meaning “Daybreak, Dawn” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Asit usually hope their child will grow to embody daybreak, dawn and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the dawn of knowledge, enlightenment, and new beginnings.

data.cultural_impact: The name Asit holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, specifically associated with the sun and the planet Venus. In Hindu astronomy, the name Asit is given to the planet Venus when it is in its beneficial aspect. It is also considered auspicious to name a child Asit during the time when the planet Venus is in its dominating position; this is believed to bring good fortune, wealth, and prosperity to the child's life.
data.spiritual_significance: Asit, a name deeply rooted in Hindu mythology, carries profound spiritual significance. According to Hindu belief, Sun (Surya) is the source of energy and life for the entire universe. Asit, as a name of the sun god, represents the divine energy and light within an individual. It's a reminder that each one of us possesses the same divine light as the sun, and can illuminate our inner world with wisdom, love, and understanding.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Asit is a Sanskrit name meaning 'dawn'. It symbolizes the auspicious beginning of a new day, filled with hope and potential. The name is also associated with Lord Ashtavakra, who embodies wisdom and enlightenment, representing the inner light that illuminates the path towards self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Asit is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as the name of a sage and a charioteer of the god Indra.
Asit is also identified with the constellation Auriga (the Charioteer), which is associated with the god Indra in Hindu astronomy and mythology.
